text.p: Maintenance at Kennecott's Utah Copper flash converting furnace, shut since April 15, is continuing and was expected to last about six weeks, company spokesman Louie Cononelos said.
The existing anode wheel caster is being replaced by a Wenmec caster, and the flash converting furnace itself is also being rebuilt.
"We are going to continue to run the flash smelting furnace for most of the shutdown," Cononelos said.

The flash smelting furnace produces matte, some of which will be stockpiled, the rest sold. "In the latter part of the shutdown we will take the flash smelting furnace down for a few days," Cononelos added.

The refinery is producing cathode from stockpile anode and was expected to continue operating during the whole of the flash converting furnace shutdown, though Cononelos was unable to say if cathode output levels will be affected.
The mine and concentrator at Bingham Canyon was working flat out, Cononelos said.
Problems at the new 270,000 tonnes per year smelter have cost the company millions of dollars in lost profits after a delay of more than a year to reach full output.
